primary_diagnosis_treated: Diabetic nephropathy (CKD stage 4) with hypertension and type 2 diabetes
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.duration: Lifelong – review annually and after eGFR or potassium changes
medications.purpose: Control hypertension and reduce proteinuria in CKD stage 4
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 recommends ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with hypertension or ACR ≥30 mg/mmol

medications.dose: 20 mg orally once daily in the evening
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CVD risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 recommends a statin for all CKD patients for CVD risk reduction

medications.dose: 0.1 units/kg subcutaneously once daily (e.g., 5 U for a 50 kg patient) titrated to fasting glucose 4–7 mmol/L
medications.purpose: Glycaemic control; metformin contraindicated at eGFR < 30 mL/min
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 advises diabetes management; insulin is appropriate when metformin is contraindicated

medications.dose: 200 mg orally once daily on an empty stomach
medications.duration: Until ferritin >100 µg/L or transferrin saturation >20% (reassess in 4 weeks)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 recommends iron supplementation for CKD‑related anemia after iron studies

contraindications.reason: eGFR 10.5 mL/min < 30 mL/min – risk of lactic acidosis
CKD stage 4 – accelerate progression and cause fluid retention
Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury in CKD
Guideline requires eGFR ≥20 mL/min for CKD indication; patient eGFR 10.5 mL/min
contraindications.alternative: None currently; focus on ACE‑I and glycaemic control

contraindications.reason: Nephrotoxic in CKD; patient has advanced CKD

assumptions_warnings: Blood pressure reading not provided – assume hypertension uncontrolled; will monitor and titrate antihypertensives as needed.
Serum potassium and creatinine baseline not available – must obtain before starting Ramipril and repeat 1–2 weeks after dose changes.
Liver function tests not available – must obtain before initiating Atorvastatin.
Lipid profile (LDL‑C, total cholesterol) not available – will order to confirm need for statin dose escalation.
Urine ACR not provided – ACE‑I indicated regardless of ACR due to hypertension, but ACR will guide BP target (<130/80 mmHg if ACR ≥70 mg/mmol).
Iron studies (ferritin, TSAT) not available – Ferrous sulfate prescribed conditionally pending results.
HbA1c and fasting glucose not provided – insulin dose will be titrated based on glucose monitoring.

treatment_summary: Start ramipril 1.25 mg daily and atorvastatin 20 mg nightly to address hypertension, proteinuria, and cardiovascular risk per NICE NG203. Metformin is contraindicated (eGFR < 30), so initiate basal insulin glargine with titration for glycaemic control. Provide oral iron pending iron studies to treat CKD‑related anemia. Avoid NSAIDs, lithium, and ACE‑I/ARB combination. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, liver enzymes, lipids, and glucose as outlined, and reassess therapy regularly.
